'''Jean Dalibard''' (born 8 December 1958) is a French [[physicist]], Professor at the [[École Polytechnique]], member of the [[French Academy of Sciences]] and a researcher at the [[École Normale Supérieure]]. 

In 2009, Dalibard received the Blaise Pascal medal of the European Academy of Sciences for "his outstanding and influential works in [[atomic physics]] and [[quantum optics]]".<ref name="eas">{{cite web|url=http://www.eurasc.org/medals/pb_medals_09.asp|title=European Academy of Sciences - Blaise Pascal Medals 2009|publisher=European Academy of Sciences|accessdate=27 June 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120627044029/http://www.eurasc.org/medals/pb_medals_09.asp|archive-date=27 June 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 2012, he received the [[Max Born Award]] and [[Davisson–Germer Prize in Atomic or Surface Physics|Davisson–Germer Prize]]. He was elected an international member of the [[American Philosophical Society]] in 2018.<ref>{{Cite web|title=APS Member History|url=https://search.amphilsoc.org/memhist/search?creator=Jean+Dalibard&title=&subject=&subdiv=&mem=&year=&year-max=&dead=&keyword=&smode=advanced|access-date=2021-02-05|website=search.amphilsoc.org}}</ref> In 2020, he was honoured to be an international member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/2020-nas-election.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200428010617/http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/2020-nas-election.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=April 28, 2020|title=2020 NAS Election}}</ref> In 2021, he was awarded the CNRS Gold Medal.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-06-24 |title=Physicist Jean Dalibard awarded the 2021 CNRS Gold Medal |url=https://www.cnrs.fr/en/press/physicist-jean-dalibard-awarded-2021-cnrs-gold-medal |access-date=2025-10-01 |website=www.cnrs.fr |language=en}}</ref>
